name: Factions and Elders of the Zealots (Libellus Sanguinis II Lore)

text.content: Calling themselves the "most renowned" of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}, the Praedicanda are the ancient Hellenic elders who abandoned the city-states of Greece to mortal and Roman rule rather than continue what they had come to see as merely a millennium-long social experiment. They dwell chiefly in Attica and Laconica, gathering annually at the mountain fortress of Acrocorinthus near Corinth to debate matters that invariably get tabled until the next meeting. Their vast libraries of Hellenic and occult lore — rumored to include hidden @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri} writings and dark sorceries kept from outsiders — draw scholars from across the clan and beyond, even as their perceived cowardice during the fall of Carthage and their aloof unwillingness to re-engage with the wider Jyhad alienate much of the clan's younger generation.

Few in number but formidable wherever they appear, the Dedicated pursue Entelechy — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} ideal of perfected mind and body — far beyond what the rest of the clan considers reasonable, organizing their pursuit around the Hellenic virtues of enkrateia (inner strength), andreia (courage), and sophrosyne (self-control). Sire and childe retreat from civilization together for decades of brutal physical and mental training; those judged to have failed to improve sufficiently are destroyed outright. A newly recognized Dedicated @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} emerges from exile to seek out and subordinate whatever clanmates he can find, by presence or by trial of strength, treating lesser @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} as inferiors to be directed rather than brothers to be persuaded. Rumors of Infernalism dog the sect, though those who have spoken with the Dedicated — including one who called himself Mandari — describe their motives as more obscure than diabolical, revolving around an enemy or purpose they never fully disclose even to allies.

In England, the anarchic @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} known as the Agitators represent the clan's newest and most undisciplined generation, having discarded the training hall's master-student tradition for undirected swordplay and open banditry. Led by Robin Leeland, they have allied with outlaw Saxon nobility against Norman rule and against the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Mithras, whose rising power in London has only sharpened their fury even as it puts them at greater risk. Preying on brigands for practice and on the Patricians' mortal herds for spite, the Agitators are, by the clan's own admission, currently more a thorn in the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} lion's paw than a genuine threat — and their raids may cost them more than they cost their targets.

A learned @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} elder and philosopher whose teachings on the clan's history, its Hellenic heritage, and the meaning of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} Ideal shape the worldview of at least one sire quoted extensively in @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} circles alike. Alypius is remembered as a source of clan lore concerning the tragedy of Hellas and the fall of Carthage, and his interpretations — particularly his suspicion that the clan's deepest rage stems from the Praedicanda's betrayal of Hellas rather than the destruction of Carthage — continue to circulate among Brujah seeking to understand the roots of the schism between the clan's young and old.

vtmlarp.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Three: Zealots
